Answer: A-ii, B-i, C-iv, D-iii.
The trap: pairing Trichoderma with insect control — it targets FUNGI, not insects.
Q4 [NEET high-difficulty] — assertion-reason

A: Baculoviruses are especially suitable for ecologically sensitive areas under IPM. R: They are species-specific, narrow-spectrum agents that do not harm plants, mammals, birds, fish, or non-target insects. Answer: (a).
The tempting wrong answer is (b): students accept both lines but doubt the causal link — when in fact the species-specificity IS the reason for the ecological suitability.
Four places this subtopic leaks marks
Pitfall 1 — Nitrogen/phosphorus mix-up. Writing "Glomus fixes nitrogen" is the single most common error. Bacteria and cyanobacteria → nitrogen; Glomus/mycorrhiza (fungus) → phosphorus.
Pitfall 2 — Symbiotic vs free-living. Rhizobium needs a legume host (symbiotic); Azotobacter and Azospirillum are free-living. NEET pair questions hinge on this exact distinction.
Pitfall 3 — Crediting Azolla instead of its symbiont. Azolla is the fern; the actual nitrogen-fixer is the cyanobacterium Anabaena azollae living in its leaf cavities.
Pitfall 4 — "Biocontrol = total kill." It does not eradicate; it keeps pests at a manageable level. And Trichoderma fights fungi, not insects.
Pro-tip — sort into three buckets first
BIOCONTROL: Bt, Trichoderma, Baculovirus, ladybird. N-FIXER: Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azospirillum, Anabaena, Nostoc. P-SUPPLIER: Glomus/mycorrhiza.
Deciding the bucket eliminates two or three options before you finish reading.
Microbes in Human Welfare — quick recall

HOUSEHOLD. Curd: Lactobacillus (LAB) → lactose to lactic acid → coagulates casein → sets curd; bonus ↑ vitamin B12, checks harmful microbes. Dough/bread/idli/dosa: Saccharomyces cerevisiae → CO2 → leavening. Toddy: fermented palm sap. Swiss cheese: big holes = large CO2 from Propionibacterium sharmanii (bacterium). Roquefort: flavour = ripened by Penicillium roqueforti (fungus). Also fermented: fish, soybean, bamboo-shoots.

INDUSTRIAL — beverages & antibiotics. Saccharomyces cerevisiae ferments malt/juice → ethanol. Wine, beer = WITHOUT distillation; whisky, brandy, rum = WITH. Antibiotic = a microbe-made chemical that kills/retards other microbes. Penicillin = first; Fleming discovered it (from Penicillium notatum); Chain & Florey developed it; Nobel 1945.

INDUSTRIAL — acids, enzymes, drugs. Aspergillus niger → citric; Acetobacter aceti → acetic; Clostridium butylicum → butyric; Lactobacillus → lactic. Lipase → detergents; pectinase/protease → juice clarification; streptokinase (Streptococcus, GM) → clot buster. Cyclosporin A (Trichoderma polysporum) → immunosuppressant for transplants; statins (Monascus purpureus) → lower cholesterol by competitively inhibiting the cholesterol-synthesis enzyme.

SEWAGE. Sewage = municipal waste water (organic matter + microbes, many pathogenic). Primary = PHYSICAL: filtration + sedimentation → effluent. Secondary = BIOLOGICAL: aeration tank, air pumped in, aerobic microbes form flocs, eat organic matter → BOD drops sharply. BOD = oxygen consumed to oxidise all organic matter in 1 L; high BOD = highly polluted. Activated sludge: small part → inoculum back to aeration; major part → anaerobic digester → biogas.

BIOGAS. A mixture of gases, predominantly methane; common name gobar gas. Methanogens = anaerobic bacteria (e.g. Methanobacterium) growing on cellulosic matter. Found in anaerobic sewage sludge and the rumen of cattle — hence dung is rich in them. Plant: inlet → sealed digester → floating gas holder → gas outlet; spent slurry → manure. Developed in India by IARI and KVIC.

BIOCONTROL. Living pest control; aim = MANAGE, not eradicate. Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis): dried spores → eaten by larva → alkaline gut activates protoxin → toxin → gut cells lyse → caterpillar dies; non-target insects spared. Gene = cry (also in Bt cotton). Trichoderma (fungus) → controls fungal plant pathogens. Baculovirus (Nucleopolyhedrovirus) → species-specific viral insecticide; ideal for IPM.

BIOFERTILISERS. Living soil enrichers; part of organic farming. Nitrogen-fixers: Rhizobium (symbiotic, legume nodules); Azotobacter, Azospirillum (free-living); cyanobacteria Anabaena/Nostoc/Oscillatoria (paddy); Azolla + Anabaena azollae. Phosphorus supplier: mycorrhiza, genus Glomus — also gives drought/salinity tolerance and root-pathogen resistance.

MEMORY AIDS. "ACID, GAS, FLAVOUR" · Bacterium = Big holes; Fungus = Flavour · "niger is the nice guy" (citric); "Monascus Minimises cholesterol" · Beer & wine Bypass the still · "Primary = Physical; Secondary = Stuff-eating" · "High BOD = Bad Old Dirty water" · "Methanogens: no air, make methane"; Rumen → Dung → Digester → Gas · "N from the bugs, P from the fungus" · "Rhizobium Rests in Roots"; Azoto/Azospirillum are Adrift · Bt = "Alkaline gut, then kaput".
One chapter, one idea: put microbes to work — in the kitchen, the fermentor, the tank, the digester, and the field.

segments.text: First, a C B S E board short answer worth three marks. Two commands: explain the mechanism, and explain the specificity.
The question: explain how Bacillus thuringiensis acts as a biocontrol agent against caterpillars. And why does it not harm other insects?

Mark one, the application and ingestion. B t is applied as dried spores mixed with water and sprayed on plants. When a caterpillar feeds, it ingests the toxin — which is present as an inactive protoxin. The word inactive is not optional; it sets up the next mark.

Mark two, the activation. The alkaline p H of the caterpillar's gut activates it into the toxic form, which damages the gut cells and kills the larva. Protoxin, then alkaline gut, then active toxin, then dead larva.

Mark three, the specificity — and this is the one students leave out. It does not harm other insects because activation and action are specific: insects lacking the right alkaline gut conditions and the right binding sites are simply unaffected.

So the full-marks tip has three parts. Name the organism in italics. State protoxin, activated by alkaline gut p H. And explicitly mention species-specificity — the question asked why, so answer the why.
Now a C U E T single-correct M C Q, and the whole question hinges on one split.
Look at the board. Three organisms in blue, one in amber. Read the stem, find the odd colour, and you are done.

The question: which one of the following supplies phosphorus to plants rather than fixing nitrogen? The answer is c, Glomus — it forms mycorrhiza and absorbs phosphorus, passing it to the plant. And the distractors are simply the blue column: Rhizobium, Anabaena, and Azospirillum are all nitrogen-fixers. The whole question is the nitrogen-versus-phosphorus split, and nothing else.
Now a N E E T match-the-column — the format this subtopic lives in. And the method is the pro-tip: bucket first, then map.
Look at the board. Each organism has its bucket printed under it. Biocontrol, N-fixer, P-supplier. Once the bucket is decided, most of the options eliminate themselves.
Column one: A, Trichoderma. B, Rhizobium. C, Glomus. D, Baculovirus.
Column two: i, symbiotic nitrogen fixation in legume nodules. ii, biocontrol of fungal plant pathogens. iii, species-specific viral insecticide. iv, phosphorus uptake via mycorrhiza.

The answer is A with two, B with one, C with four, D with three. Trichoderma is the mycoparasitic fungus controlling other fungi. Rhizobium is the symbiotic nitrogen-fixer in legume nodules. Glomus is the mycorrhizal phosphorus supplier. And baculovirus, Nucleopolyhedrovirus, is the narrow-spectrum viral insecticide.

And the trap is the one we flagged earlier: pairing Trichoderma with insect control. It targets fungi, not insects. Notice how tempting that is — three of the four agents here deal with animals, so the fungus-fights-fungus row feels out of place. It is not.
Now the hardest format, and it rewards understanding rather than recall.

Assertion: baculoviruses are especially suitable for use in ecologically sensitive areas under Integrated Pest Management. Reason: baculoviruses are species-specific, narrow-spectrum agents that do not harm plants, mammals, birds, fish, or non-target insects. The answer is a — both true, and R correctly explains A.

<curious> And here is why good students slip. The tempting wrong answer is b. They accept both lines happily, then doubt the causal link. But think about it: their narrowness is exactly what makes them ideal where broad-spectrum chemicals would cause collateral ecological damage. The species-specificity is the reason for the ecological suitability. There is no gap to prise open.
This subtopic has shallow reasoning but unforgiving mapping — so every pitfall here is a swapped name. Four of them.

Pitfall one: the nitrogen and phosphorus mix-up. Writing that Glomus fixes nitrogen is the single most common error in this subtopic. Bacteria and cyanobacteria give nitrogen. Glomus — mycorrhiza, a fungus — gives phosphorus. N from the bugs, P from the fungus.

Pitfall two: symbiotic versus free-living. Rhizobium needs a legume host, so it is symbiotic. Azotobacter and Azospirillum are free-living. N E E T pair questions — which pair consists only of free-living nitrogen-fixers — hinge on this exact distinction. Rhizobium Rests in Roots; the Azo twins are Adrift.

Pitfall three: crediting Azolla instead of its symbiont. Azolla is the fern. The actual nitrogen-fixer is the cyanobacterium Anabaena azollae, living in its leaf cavities. The fern gets the fame; the cyanobacterium does the work.

Pitfall four: thinking biocontrol means total kill. It does not eradicate; it keeps pests at a manageable level through checks and balances. And in the same breath: Trichoderma fights fungi, not insects. Both of these are conceptual traps, not memory traps.
<whisper> Now the pro-tip, and it is the same discipline that carried you through the household products subtopic.

In any match-the-column or odd-one-out, first sort each organism into one of three buckets. Biocontrol: B t, Trichoderma, baculovirus, ladybird beetle. Nitrogen-fixer: Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azospirillum, Anabaena, Nostoc. Phosphorus-supplier: Glomus, mycorrhiza.

Deciding the bucket eliminates two or three options before you finish reading them. Bucket first, then map. That is the whole technique — and on the most name-heavy subtopic in the chapter, technique beats memory every time.
<excited> Right — the whole chapter, on one board. This is your revision section. Do not learn it here; use it to check what has already stuck.

Household products. Curd: Lactobacillus, the L A B, turns lactose into lactic acid, which coagulates casein and sets the curd — with a bonus of more vitamin B twelve and harmful microbes checked. Dough, bread, idli, dosa: Saccharomyces cerevisiae gives carbon dioxide, which leavens. Toddy is fermented palm sap. Swiss cheese: the big holes are large carbon dioxide from Propionibacterium sharmanii, a bacterium. Roquefort: the flavour is ripening by Penicillium roqueforti, a fungus. And microbes also ferment fish, soybean, and bamboo-shoots.

Industrial products, first half. Saccharomyces cerevisiae ferments malt or juice to ethanol. Wine and beer without distillation; whisky, brandy, and rum with it. An antibiotic is a microbe-made chemical that kills or retards other microbes. Penicillin was the first, discovered by Fleming from Penicillium notatum, developed into a drug by Chain and Florey, and the Nobel came in nineteen forty-five.

Industrial products, second half — the ledger. Aspergillus niger gives citric acid; Acetobacter aceti, acetic; Clostridium butylicum, butyric; Lactobacillus, lactic. Lipase goes to detergents; pectinase and protease to juice clarification; streptokinase, from Streptococcus and genetically modified, is the clot buster. Cyclosporin A from Trichoderma polysporum prevents transplant rejection; statins from Monascus purpureus lower cholesterol by competitively inhibiting the cholesterol-synthesis enzyme.

Sewage treatment. Primary is physical — filtration and sedimentation, giving effluent. Secondary is biological — the aeration tank, air pumped in, aerobic microbes forming flocs and eating the organic matter, so the B O D drops sharply. B O D is the oxygen consumed to oxidise all the organic matter in one litre; high B O D means heavily polluted. And the activated sludge has two fates: a small part back to aeration as inoculum, the major part to the anaerobic digester, giving biogas.

Biogas. A mixture of gases, predominantly methane — gobar gas. Methanogens are anaerobic bacteria, Methanobacterium the example, growing on cellulosic matter. They live in anaerobic sewage sludge and in the rumen of cattle, which is why dung is rich in them. The plant: inlet, sealed digester, floating gas holder, gas outlet — and the spent slurry goes out as manure. Developed in India by I A R I and K V I C.

Biocontrol. Living pest control, and the aim is to manage, not eradicate. B t: dried spores, eaten by the larva, the alkaline gut activates the protoxin, the toxin lyses the gut cells, the caterpillar dies — and non-target insects are spared. The gene is cry, the same one in B t cotton. Trichoderma, a fungus, controls fungal plant pathogens. Baculovirus is the species-specific viral insecticide, ideal for I P M.

Biofertilisers. Nitrogen-fixers: Rhizobium, symbiotic in legume nodules; Azotobacter and Azospirillum, free-living; the cyanobacteria Anabaena, Nostoc, Oscillatoria in paddy; and Azolla with Anabaena azollae. Phosphorus supplier: mycorrhiza, genus Glomus — which also gives drought and salinity tolerance, and root-pathogen resistance.

And the memory aids, all in one place. Acid, gas, flavour. Bacterium equals big holes; fungus equals flavour. Niger is the nice guy; Monascus minimises cholesterol. Beer and wine bypass the still. Primary is physical; secondary is stuff-eating. High B O D is bad, old, dirty water. Methanogens: no air, make methane — rumen, dung, digester, gas. N from the bugs, P from the fungus. Rhizobium rests in roots; the Azo twins are adrift. And B t: alkaline gut, then kaput.

One chapter, one idea. Every section here is the same move: put microbes to work. In the kitchen, in the fermentor, in the tank, in the digester, and in the field. Learn the organism, learn what it hands back, and this chapter pays you every single year.
पहले, एक C B S E board short answer, तीन marks का। दो commands: mechanism समझाइए, और specificity समझाइए।
Question: समझाइए कि Bacillus thuringiensis caterpillars के ख़िलाफ़ biocontrol agent की तरह कैसे काम करता है। और ये दूसरे कीड़ों को नुक़सान क्यों नहीं पहुँचाता?

Mark one, छिड़काव और निगलना। B t को dried spores के रूप में पानी में मिलाकर पौधों पर छिड़का जाता है। जब caterpillar खाता है, तो वो toxin निगल लेता है — जो एक inactive protoxin के रूप में मौजूद है। Inactive शब्द वैकल्पिक नहीं है; वही अगला mark तैयार करता है।

Mark two, activation। Caterpillar की gut का alkaline p H उसे toxic रूप में activate कर देता है, जो gut cells को नुक़सान पहुँचाकर larva को मार देता है। Protoxin, फिर alkaline gut, फिर active toxin, फिर मरा हुआ larva।

Mark three, specificity — और यही वो है जिसे students छोड़ देते हैं। ये दूसरे कीड़ों को नुक़सान इसलिए नहीं पहुँचाता क्योंकि activation और action दोनों specific हैं: जिन कीड़ों के पास सही alkaline gut conditions और सही binding sites नहीं हैं, उन पर कोई असर ही नहीं होता।

तो full-marks tip के तीन हिस्से हैं। Organism italics में लिखिए। Protoxin और alkaline gut p H से activation लिखिए। और species-specificity का साफ़-साफ़ ज़िक्र कीजिए — question ने why पूछा है, तो why का जवाब दीजिए।
अब एक C U E T single-correct M C Q, और पूरा question एक ही split पर टिका है।
Board देखिए। तीन organisms नीले, एक अंबर। Stem पढ़िए, अलग रंग ढूँढिए, और काम ख़त्म।

Question: इनमें से कौन पौधों को phosphorus देता है, nitrogen fix करने के बजाय? जवाब है c, Glomus — ये mycorrhiza बनाता है और phosphorus सोखकर पौधे को देता है। और distractors बस वही नीला column हैं: Rhizobium, Anabaena, और Azospirillum, सब nitrogen-fixers हैं। पूरा question वही nitrogen-versus-phosphorus split है, और कुछ नहीं।
अब एक N E E T match-the-column — वही format जिसमें ये subtopic जीता है। और तरीक़ा वही pro-tip है: पहले bucket, फिर map।
Board देखिए। हर organism के नीचे उसका bucket छपा है। Biocontrol, N-fixer, P-supplier। एक बार bucket तय हुआ, तो ज़्यादातर options ख़ुद ही हट जाते हैं।
Column one: A, Trichoderma। B, Rhizobium। C, Glomus। D, Baculovirus।
Column two: i, legume nodules में symbiotic nitrogen fixation। ii, fungal plant pathogens का biocontrol। iii, species-specific viral insecticide। iv, mycorrhiza के ज़रिए phosphorus uptake।

Answer है A with two, B with one, C with four, D with three। Trichoderma वो mycoparasitic fungus है जो दूसरे fungi को control करता है। Rhizobium legume nodules का symbiotic nitrogen-fixer है। Glomus mycorrhizal phosphorus supplier है। और baculovirus, यानी Nucleopolyhedrovirus, narrow-spectrum viral insecticide है।

और trap वही है जो हमने पहले चिह्नित किया था: Trichoderma को insect control के साथ जोड़ देना। वो fungi को निशाना बनाता है, कीड़ों को नहीं। ग़ौर कीजिए ये कितना ललचाने वाला है — यहाँ के चार में से तीन agents जानवरों से निपटते हैं, तो fungus-fights-fungus वाली row बेमेल लगती है। है नहीं।
अब सबसे मुश्किल format, और ये recall नहीं, समझ को इनाम देता है।

Assertion: baculoviruses Integrated Pest Management के तहत ecologically sensitive इलाक़ों के लिए ख़ासतौर पर उपयुक्त हैं। Reason: baculoviruses species-specific, narrow-spectrum agents हैं जो पौधों, mammals, पक्षियों, मछलियों, या non-target कीड़ों को नुक़सान नहीं पहुँचाते। Answer है a — दोनों सही, और R ही A का correct explanation है।

<curious> और यहीं अच्छे students फिसलते हैं। Tempting ग़लत जवाब है b। वो दोनों lines ख़ुशी से मान लेते हैं, फिर causal link पर शक करने लगते हैं। लेकिन सोचिए: उनका संकरापन ही वो चीज़ है जो उन्हें वहाँ ideal बनाती है जहाँ broad-spectrum chemicals ज़मानत भर का पारिस्थितिक नुक़सान कर देते। Species-specificity ही ecological suitability की वजह है। बीच में कोई दरार है ही नहीं जिसे चौड़ा किया जा सके।
इस subtopic में reasoning उथली है पर mapping बेरहम — तो यहाँ का हर pitfall एक बदला हुआ नाम है। चार हैं।

Pitfall one: nitrogen और phosphorus की अदला-बदली। ये लिखना कि Glomus nitrogen fix करता है — इस subtopic की सबसे common ग़लती यही है। Bacteria और cyanobacteria nitrogen देते हैं। Glomus — mycorrhiza, एक fungus — phosphorus देता है। N from the bugs, P from the fungus।

Pitfall two: symbiotic बनाम free-living। Rhizobium को legume host चाहिए, इसलिए वो symbiotic है। Azotobacter और Azospirillum free-living हैं। N E E T के pair questions — कौन सी जोड़ी सिर्फ़ free-living nitrogen-fixers की है — ठीक इसी distinction पर टिके होते हैं। Rhizobium Rests in Roots; Azo जुड़वाँ Adrift हैं।

Pitfall three: Azolla को श्रेय दे देना, उसके symbiont को नहीं। Azolla fern है। असली nitrogen-fixer है cyanobacterium Anabaena azollae, जो उसकी leaf cavities में रहता है। नाम fern का होता है; काम cyanobacterium करता है।

Pitfall four: ये समझना कि biocontrol मतलब पूरी सफ़ाई। वो eradicate नहीं करता; वो checks and balances से pests को manageable level पर रखता है। और साथ ही: Trichoderma fungi से लड़ता है, कीड़ों से नहीं। ये दोनों conceptual traps हैं, memory के traps नहीं।

किसी भी match-the-column या odd-one-out में, पहले हर organism को तीन buckets में से एक में डालिए। Biocontrol: B t, Trichoderma, baculovirus, ladybird beetle। Nitrogen-fixer: Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azospirillum, Anabaena, Nostoc। Phosphorus-supplier: Glomus, mycorrhiza।

Bucket तय कर लेने से दो या तीन options तभी हट जाते हैं जब आपने उन्हें पूरा पढ़ा भी नहीं होता। पहले bucket, फिर map। यही पूरी technique है — और chapter के सबसे name-heavy subtopic पर technique हर बार memory को हरा देती है।

Household products। Curd: Lactobacillus, यानी L A B, lactose को lactic acid में बदलता है, जो casein को coagulate करके curd जमा देता है — bonus में ज़्यादा vitamin B twelve और harmful microbes का check। Dough, bread, idli, dosa: Saccharomyces cerevisiae carbon dioxide देता है, जो leavening करती है। Toddy fermented palm sap है। Swiss cheese: बड़े holes Propionibacterium sharmanii, एक bacterium, की बड़ी मात्रा वाली carbon dioxide से। Roquefort: flavour Penicillium roqueforti, एक fungus, की ripening से। और microbes fish, soybean, तथा bamboo-shoots को भी ferment करते हैं।

Industrial products, पहला आधा। Saccharomyces cerevisiae malt या juice को ferment करके ethanol बनाता है। Wine और beer without distillation; whisky, brandy, rum with distillation। Antibiotic वो microbe-made chemical है जो दूसरे microbes को मारता या रोकता है। Penicillin पहला था, Fleming ने Penicillium notatum से discover किया, Chain और Florey ने drug बनाया, और Nobel मिला उन्नीस सौ पैंतालीस में।

Industrial products, दूसरा आधा — वो ledger। Aspergillus niger citric acid देता है; Acetobacter aceti, acetic; Clostridium butylicum, butyric; Lactobacillus, lactic। Lipase detergents में; pectinase और protease juice clarification में; streptokinase, Streptococcus से और genetically modified, clot buster है। Trichoderma polysporum से cyclosporin A transplant rejection रोकता है; Monascus purpureus से statins cholesterol-synthesis enzyme को competitively inhibit करके cholesterol घटाते हैं।

Sewage treatment। Primary physical है — filtration और sedimentation, जिससे effluent मिलता है। Secondary biological है — aeration tank, हवा pump होती है, aerobic microbes flocs बनाकर organic matter खाते हैं, तो B O D तेज़ी से गिरता है। B O D वो oxygen है जो एक litre के सारे organic matter को oxidise करने में खर्च हो। ऊँचा B O D मतलब बहुत प्रदूषित। और activated sludge के दो अंजाम: छोटा हिस्सा inoculum बनकर aeration में वापस, बड़ा हिस्सा anaerobic digester में, जिससे biogas।

Biogas। Gases का mixture, predominantly methane — gobar gas। Methanogens anaerobic bacteria हैं, example Methanobacterium, जो cellulosic matter पर उगते हैं। ये anaerobic sewage sludge और cattle के rumen में रहते हैं, इसीलिए dung इनसे भरपूर होता है। Plant: inlet, sealed digester, floating gas holder, gas outlet — और spent slurry manure बनकर बाहर। भारत में I A R I और K V I C ने विकसित किया।

Biocontrol। ज़िंदा pest control, और मक़सद manage करना है, eradicate नहीं। B t: dried spores, larva खाता है, alkaline gut protoxin को activate करती है, toxin gut cells को lyse कर देता है, caterpillar मर जाता है — और non-target कीड़े बच जाते हैं। Gene है cry, वही जो B t cotton में है। Trichoderma, एक fungus, fungal plant pathogens को control करता है। Baculovirus species-specific viral insecticide है, I P M के लिए ideal।

Biofertilisers। Nitrogen-fixers: Rhizobium, legume nodules में symbiotic; Azotobacter और Azospirillum, free-living; cyanobacteria Anabaena, Nostoc, Oscillatoria paddy में; और Azolla के साथ Anabaena azollae। Phosphorus supplier: mycorrhiza, genus Glomus — जो drought और salinity tolerance, तथा root-pathogen resistance भी देता है।

और memory aids, सब एक जगह। Acid, gas, flavour। Bacterium मतलब big holes; fungus मतलब flavour। Niger is the nice guy; Monascus minimises cholesterol। Beer और wine bypass the still। Primary is physical; secondary is stuff-eating। High B O D is bad, old, dirty water। Methanogens: no air, make methane — rumen, dung, digester, gas। N from the bugs, P from the fungus। Rhizobium rests in roots; Azo जुड़वाँ adrift हैं। और B t: alkaline gut, then kaput।

एक chapter, एक idea। यहाँ का हर section वही एक चाल है: microbes को काम पर लगा दो। रसोई में, fermentor में, tank में, digester में, और खेत में। Organism सीखिए, और सीखिए कि वो बदले में क्या थमाता है — फिर ये chapter आपको हर साल चुकाता रहेगा।
